newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end sharply lower on fund selling, stops.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end sharply lower on fund selling, stops.

text.p: Concern over cash pork product movement weighed on the market but most of the late break and sharp lower close in CME hog futures came from fund liquidation, traders said.

Hog futures finished 0.700 to 1.500 cents per lb lower with June off the least and July off 1.200 at 80.150 cents. Pork bellies ended mostly 0.875 lower to 0.500 higher with July off 0.825 at 83.675 cents.
Local pressure prompted by further weakness in the cash pork complex took futures down into technical sell stops and funds liquidated positions into the close, traders said.

Much of the local selling came despite floor talk that cash hog markets could be steady to firm much of the week due to light hog marketings. Hog calls turned mixed later and futures broke as the cash pork complex was acting weaker than expected, they said.

"Some of these traders were getting tired of waiting" for word from Japan on their expected pork buying, said Dave Maher from Securities Corporation of Iowa. "We're now into the second week of June and still haven't heard a thing."
This kept buyers out of the futures market and prompted light selling which took prices down, traders said.

Added pressure in deferreds stemmed from expectations of increased hog supplies going into next year. The next Hogs and Pigs report is due out at the end of June and it is expected to show stepped up production of hogs ahead, they said.

Rand Financials, Rosenthal Collins and LFG bought early but Rosenthal turned seller along with locals. R.J. O'Brien and Lind-Waldock sold early while ABN Chicogo Corp and Smith Barney sold late. E.D.&F. Man bought July and sold June early, thought to be rolling. Fimat Futures USA bought August and sold July early and Refco did that spread late, thought to be further 'Goldman roll", pit sources said.
In hog options, LFG sold October 68 and 70 puts, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures rallied from lows late on local short covering and buying by Dean Witter but held losses in nearbys on pressure from lower cash and a weak technical picture. Sell stops were hit under 84.000 cents in July early as prices moved to lowest levels since mid April, traders said.
Early underlying support came from ideas Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town storage report may show a net out-movement last week versus an in-movement last year, they said.
LFG sold on the break after buying early. E.D.&F. Man sold early, pit sources said.
